The Honorable Rogers C. Morton U. S. Department of the Interior
Page 5 August 4, 1972
3. A problem currently being created by land closures is a higher concentration of use is being experienced by those areas which remain open which in turn auguments any problems that might be created by over-use. Therefore, very thorough consideration must be given to any closure of the public domain.
4. A reevaluation is in order of the types of recreation which are in one way or another subsidized by the government in relation to the numbers of people involved in various recreational pursuits.
5. The Bureau of Land Management should reevaluate their leasing practices of public lands for sheep and cattle grazing and mining operations. To prevent such unfair practices as "checkerboard leasing", current practices allow a lessee to lease sections of land which are diagonally adjacent to one another in a "checkerboard" pattern without paying for the lease rights on those sections of land which become entrapped by surrounding leaseholds. This practice allows leaseholders to monopolize 100% more land than they actually pay rental on and gives them the right to deny tresspass privileges to the general public.
6. An immediate and inexpensive solution to the problem of over-crowded existing recreation areas might be a rescheduling of vacation periods in the schools of our country. By requiring approximately 25% of the student bodies to vacation during each of four quarters annually, we would not only eliminate the summer vacation conjection but would make better use of our educational facilities as well.
7. A very effective program which was instituted by the government during the late 1930s under the banner of 'CCC' might be revitalized to assist in building new and rehabilitating our existing recreation facilities across the country while making use of the very large unemployed labor force which is currently available. Since through various welfare and unemployment compensation plans we, the taxpayers, support the unemployed while they are idle, it would make economical sense to accomplish some worthwhile end while supporting these people.
8. When conflicts occur between various groups interested in the use of a specific tract of land, we feel that the best solution is to call together the representatives from those interested groups and allow them to work out their differences in a democratic manner. The government body responsible for the operation and administration of the area in question should be called upon to moderate any arbitration of this type. Trailer Coach Association strongly believes in the theory of self-government and therefore feels that the people who are directly involved in the results of regulation are entitled to a say in the writing and implementation of those regulations.
